ai_summary:
Great Britain is currently recording 6.7 GW of wind output, with estimated Scottish wind generation delivering 3.6 GW, representing 35.6% of Scotland's installed Scottish wind capacity. This abundant renewable output allows Scotland to maintain a carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide carbon intensity of 168 gCO2/kWh. Despite this clean generation, structural transmission limitations continue to prevent power from flowing south where demand is highest. 

Consequently, 17.5 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, accumulating a direct constraint cost of about £586,363. To compensate for this stranded green energy, fossil generation stepped in, resulting in an estimated 3,333,550 m3 of natural gas burned elsewhere on the grid and producing 6,141 tonnes of avoidable CO2 emissions. Extrapolating today’s constraint expenditure yields an estimated total yearly cost of £214 million. When socialized across national balancing mechanism charges, this curtailment is estimated to increase everybody’s invoice in the UK by approximately £1/MWh, highlighting the dual economic and environmental toll of transmission bottlenecks.
